processing: A green tea with the enzymes fixed by heat, shaped into a curved hook; made to provincial tea production rules.
harvest_season: Exact dates are little documented; spring is the usual prized picking for Guizhou greens.
taste_profile: Strong chestnut aroma over a mellow, full body, with a sweet finish that comes back after swallowing.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a Chinese green. A slightly hotter steep suits the chestnut character, but back off if it turns bitter.

vintage_note: It follows the usual pattern for its class: current-year spring harvest, best within about a year. It is not sold by vintage, and the tribute name refers to local history, not to age or a higher grade.
description:
Jinsha Gongcha is the registered regional tea of Jinsha County in northwest Guizhou. The word gongcha means tribute tea, and the county leans on that story heavily.

The finished green is curved like a fish hook, downy and glossy. Beyond that, little is published about its specific method, other than that producers work to provincial tea production rules, so assume ordinary green tea steps of heat fixing, shaping and drying.

In the cup, the registered description points to chestnut aroma, a mellow body and a sweet return. Treat it as a chestnut-leaning Chinese green: water just under boiling, modest steeps, and a clean porcelain cup to catch the aroma.

The word tribute is no guarantee of anything, so judge it by the leaf and the picking date.
history:
Local accounts make very large claims. They trace tribute tea here to the Han dynasty, naming the envoy Tang Meng and an order from Emperor Wu in 135 BC, and continuing to the Jiaqing reign of the Qing. Treat this as local tradition, and the claim that Jinsha is the birthplace of tribute tea is promotional.

The county also reports more than 40 old cultivated tea trees it dates to over a thousand years. Accounts also mention sales of the tea in Qing times, and the county holds the modern title of China's home of tribute tea from the China Tea Marketing Association.

The national agriculture ministry registered the name as an agricultural geographical indication on 18 November 2014, covering 26 towns and townships.
